newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany raps Belarus over human rights curbs.
newsitem.headline: Germany raps Belarus over human rights curbs.

text.p: German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel summoned the Belarussian ambassador on Thursday to express deep concern over increasing restrictions on humanitarian organisations in the former Soviet republic.

A senior ministry official told ambassador Pyotr Belyayev the closure of the Minsk-based foundation The Children of Chernobyl which worked closely with German humanitarian groups was detrimental to ties.
The foundation was a charity organisation that helped victims of the 1986 accident in Chernobyl nuclear power station in neighbouring Ukraine which affected parts of Belarus.

"The latest curbs on the media and attempts to exert pressure on opposition politicians and reformed institutions contradict the principles which Belarus agreed to keep to and on which it bases its relations with Germany and the rest of the European Union," the ministry said in a statement.
The statement said Germany and the EU were prepared to support Belarus on the path to democracy on condition that it strengthened its democratic institutions.
Belarus's President Alexander Lukashenko was last year critised by the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe for using a selective referendum to expand his powers.
Lukashenko, who is popular in Belarus, argues his people simply have a different vision on these issues.
